messages.subject: legend.key versus geom_smooth (ggplot2 1.0.0)
parts:
Dear folks,

I've been using ggplot2 for a while now, and gotten some really good plots from it.  It's my default choice now, so thanks to all, especially Hadley!

But... you knew this was coming... one little thing that I can't seem to get right.  My colleagues have asked for plots with a white background (and the journal will also ask for this) so I'm using "theme_bw()" as in the following snippet:

---------------------
df <- data.frame(c(1:10,1:10),runif(20,-2,2),c(rep("alpha",times=10),rep("beta",times=10)))
colnames(df) <- c("x","y","tag")
x <- ggplot(df,aes(x=x,y=y,color=tag)) +
             geom_smooth(method="loess") +
             theme_bw()
print(x)
---------------------

but the background of the legend keys is still grey (see attached "sample_bw.pdf").  If I add "theme(legend.key = element_rect(fill="transparent"))" as in:

---------------------
x = ggplot(df,aes(x=x,y=y,color=tag)) +
             geom_smooth(method="loess") +
             theme_bw() +
             theme(legend.key = element_rect(fill="transparent"))
----------------------

then the background of the keys remains grey (see "sample_transparent.pdf").  Likewise if I set it to white (but it turns blue if I set it to "blue"...).  But... if I replace "geom_smooth" with "geom_line", then it behaves as expected (see attached "sample_line.pdf"):

---------------------
x = ggplot(df,aes(x=x,y=y,color=tag)) +
             geom_line() +
             theme_bw() +
             theme(legend.key = element_rect(fill="transparent"))
----------------------

So... what is it about "geom_smooth" that won't allow a transparent or white background for the keys, but will allow blue???  Can somebody tell me how to set the background of the key to white (or transparent) while still using "geom_smooth"?  I've tried various things, up to and including re-defining "theme_bw" manually, setting "legend.key" explicitly in the theme... no joy.  Any advice/help would be appreciated.

Many thanks...

messages.subject: Re: legend.key versus geom_smooth (ggplot2 1.0.0)
parts:
The grey in the legend isn't coming from the theme, it's coming from
the geom. Maybe try something like this:

ggplot(df,aes(x=x,y=y,color=tag)) +
geom_smooth(method="loess", se = FALSE) +
geom_smooth(method="loess", show_guide = FALSE) +
theme_bw()


Best,
Ista

messages.author: ed8631ca60fd321d
messages.subject: Re: legend.key versus geom_smooth (ggplot2 1.0.0)
parts:
Hi, Ista,

Much appreciated, that's got it, and I think I even understand why.  So, just for the record (in case another confused person reads this):

The grey background in the key is geom_smooth's way of telling me that the plot is displaying the confidence interval (in grey) around the smoothed line.  Without the confidence interval, it doesn't colour the background of the key, because the line doesn't have the grey confidence interval around it.

Must admit that was too subtle for me.  Again, thanks.

Cheers,

 - Gord
